articles.title: Zimbabwe's tobacco anchor in Britain holds at £129m
articles.description: Of every £100 of goods Zimbabwe sells to Britain, £96 is tobacco or beverages. While the wider UK–Zimbabwe trade relationship softened in the year to December 2025, Zimbabwean tobacco held its grip, and the IMF projects Zimbabwean GDP growth of 7.5% in 2025 and 5.0% in 2026. The product that built Zimbabwe's name as an exporter is still doing the work.

articles.title: The Apple of haircare gets its German cheque
articles.description: Ruka, the London-based textured-hair company founded by Zimbabwean entrepreneur Varaidzo Tendai Moyo and her co-founder Ugorji Agbai, has closed a $4.5m round co-led by Henkel Ventures and Freedom Trail Capital. The deal, which takes lifetime funding to roughly $10m and brings one of the world's largest consumer-goods groups onto the cap table, is the most meaningful endorsement yet of a Zimbabwean diaspora-founded brand.

more.title: Pardon Mapondera: gone but not forgotten at Venice
more.description: The fifth and final piece in our series on Zimbabwe's pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale. Pardon Mapondera, the artist whose practice the room finally arranges itself around, treats discarded plastic and glass jars not as ecological signal but as ritual matter, and produces, in the process, the most quietly devotional installation in the Biennale this year.

more.title: Gideon Gomo: from stone to bronze, the ancestral algorithm at Venice
more.description: The fourth in a five-part series on Zimbabwe's pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale. Gideon Gomo's first sustained body of bronze work, paired with discarded vehicle number plates and Zimbabwean springstone, is the move of a sculptor at full maturity rethinking the material vocabulary of his country's most internationally legible art form.

more.title: Shumba Maasai in Venice
more.description: At the 61st Biennale, the Zimbabwean artist's day-long procession through the city's campi, performed under the borrowed authority of a Murehwa chief, restages the social-sculpture lineage of Joseph Beuys for a contemporary African discursive practice.

more.title: Franklyn Dzingai: family albums and the neural commons at Venice
more.description: The third in a five-part series on Zimbabwe's pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale. Franklyn Dzingai's reductive cardboard prints, built from the family album, the magazine clipping, the back-room studio photographs of mid-century Zimbabwe, turn out, on close looking, to be the most precisely engineered work in the room.

more.title: Felix Shumba: charcoal and the practice of disappearance at Venice
more.description: The second in a five-part series on Zimbabwe's pavilion at the 61st Venice Biennale. Felix Shumba's six-metre charcoal wall and his Telephone Reader series anchor a body of work that argues drawing is not the act of capturing the seen, but the act of staying present to what is on its way out of sight.

more.title: UK services share in Zimbabwe rises to 8.2%
more.description: The headline UK services trade with Zimbabwe softened year on year. The structural number underneath it tells the better story: Britain's share of all services Zimbabwe imports rose 2.4 percentage points to 8.2%, the highest measured level in years. As Zimbabwean buyers re-rate their global supplier mix, the UK is taking a bigger slice of the country's services demand.

more.title: Zimbabwe's demand lifts British exports by 14.6%
more.description: The Zimbabwean economy is in its strongest stretch in years: 7.5% GDP growth in 2025, a projected 5% in 2026, and that growth is pulling demand for cars, commercial vehicles, medicines and industrial machinery in with it. UK goods exports to Zimbabwe rose 14.6% on the year, the strongest line in an otherwise soft bilateral picture for Britain.

more.title: ZGA joins nation in mourning Bosso executives
more.description: Brandon Moyo THE Zimbabwe Golf Association (ZGA) has joined the nation in mourning the tragic loss of Highlanders Football Club executives who died in a road traffic accident on Thursday evening. The accident, which occurred along the Harare-Bulawayo Road, claimed the lives of club chairman Colonel (Rtd) Kenneth Mhlophe, vice-chairman Sifiso “Fiso” Siziba, treasurer Nkani Khoza and club member Mbalenhle Sibanda. In a statement, the ZGA said it stood in solidarity with the Bosso family during this difficult period, adding that the three leaders’ dedication and contribution to football would always be remembered. “The Zimbabwe Golf Association extends its heartfelt condolences on the tragic passing of Mr Kenneth Mhlophe (Club Chairman), Mr Sifiso Siziba (Vice Chairman), and Mr Nkani Khoza (Treasurer). We stand with their families, loved ones, and the entire Highlanders FC community during this devastating period of bereavement. “Their immense dedication, leadership, and service to the club will forever be remembered. Our thoughts and prayers are also with the football fraternity and all those affected by this immense loss. May their dear souls rest in eternal peace,” read the statement. A joint memorial service to celebrate and honour the lives of the quartet will be held on Monday at Barbourfields Stadium. The four were granted State-assisted funerals in recognition of their service, with the memorial service expected to bring together family, friends, the football fraternity and members of the public to pay their final respects.

more.title: Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s secure sponsorship deal with Budget Cash & Carry
more.description: Chronicle Writer THE Young Flying Stars Sports Academy (YFSSA) under-20 side has confirmed a major sponsorship agreement with Budget Cash & Carry, a leading wholesaler based in Bulawayo. The deal, signed for an undisclosed amount, will see Budget Cash & Carry supply the team’s home kit, away kit, and third kit, while also covering travel and camp logistics for the squad. [caption id=attachment_5408316 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] This partnership represents a significant boost for the academy’s under-20 players, ensuring they are equipped with professional-standard gear and supported in their competitive development. “We are proud to partner with Young Flying Stars Sports Academy’s under-20 side, a team that embodies the future of football in Zimbabwe,” said a spokesperson for Budget Cash & Carry. [caption id=attachment_5408326 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] “Our new partnership underlines our commitment to nurturing young talent and strengthening community sport in Bulawayo. We believe this collaboration will inspire the next generation of athletes and bring fans closer to the game.” Budget Cash & Carry has also confirmed that replica jerseys will be available for parents and fans, allowing the wider community to show their support for the under-20 side both at matches and beyond. [caption id=attachment_5408331 align=aligncenter width=300] Young Flying Stars Sports Academy Under-20s[/caption] The academy’s leadership has welcomed the sponsorship as a timely boost for the under-20 side, emphasising the importance of corporate partnerships in sustaining youth football. Director Collen Nyambiya highlighted the impact the deal will have on the players and the wider community. “This partnership with Budget Cash & Carry is a milestone for our under-20 side. Their support in providing kits and funding travel logistics ensures our young players can focus entirely on their football development. It is more than just a sponsorship; it is an investment in the future of Zimbabwean football, and we are grateful for their commitment to nurturing talent at grassroots level.” The sponsorship not only enhances the academy’s resources but also highlights the importance of corporate backing in developing Zimbabwe’s next wave of football stars.
